name: Spot the leak
note: Each setup looks fine and reports a great number. Pick the leak that makes the number a lie.

items.prompt: We built our eval set by sampling from the same conversation logs the model was fine-tuned on. Accuracy is 0.96.
candidates: Train/eval overlap — the model may have seen these exact examples in training
The eval set is too small
We should have used F1 instead of accuracy
items.correct: Train/eval overlap — the model may have seen these exact examples in training
items.explanation: If eval examples (or near-duplicates) appear in the training data, the score measures memorization, not generalization. The eval set must be disjoint from training — ideally split by time or by entity so near-duplicates can't straddle the boundary.
items.principle: A test set the model trained on is not a test set.

items.prompt: Our RAG eval uses Wikipedia articles that are also in the model's pretraining corpus. Answer accuracy is high.
candidates: The model can answer from memory, so you aren't testing retrieval at all
items.correct: The model can answer from memory, so you aren't testing retrieval at all
items.explanation: When the answer is in parametric memory, the generator can be right even if retrieval returned garbage — your retrieval metrics and faithfulness are masked. Test RAG on documents the model could not have memorized (private, post-cutoff, or synthetic) to isolate the retrieval contribution.
items.principle: To test retrieval, use context the model can't already recall.

items.prompt: We've been tuning prompts against the same 500-example eval set for three months. Our score keeps climbing.
candidates: Adaptive overfitting — the eval set has effectively become training data
items.correct: Adaptive overfitting — the eval set has effectively become training data
items.explanation: Every decision you make to raise a score on a fixed set leaks information from it into your system. After enough rounds the gains are overfitting to that set, not real improvement. Keep a rotating or held-out confirmation set you touch rarely, and refresh the dev set.
items.principle: A test set you optimize against stops being a test set.
